issue_context.title: BUG: GroupBy's quantile incompatible with pd.NA
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

Firstly, here's a working example using the default dtypes:

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "x": [1, 1],
    "y": [0.2, np.nan]
})
print(f"dtypes:\n{df.dtypes}")
display(df.groupby("x")["y"].quantile(0.5))
```
<details>

```text
dtypes:
x      int64
y    float64
dtype: object
x
1    0.2
Name: y, dtype: float64
```

</details>

To contrast, if I use the Pandas dtypes, the codef ails

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "x": [1, 1],
    "y": [0.2, np.nan]
}).astype({"x": pd.Int64Dtype(), "y": pd.Float64Dtype()})
print(f"dtypes:\n{df.dtypes}")
display(df.groupby("x")["y"].quantile(0.5))
```
<details>

```text
dtypes:
x      Int64
y    Float64
dtype: object

TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a number, not 'NAType'

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
/tmp/josh/ipykernel_67869/1525766791.py in <module>
      4 }).astype({"x": pd.Int64Dtype(), "y": pd.Float64Dtype()})
      5 print(f"dtypes:\n{df.dtypes}")
----> 6 display(df.groupby("x")["y"].quantile(0.5))

.../python3.9/site-packages/pandas/core/groupby/groupby.py in quantile(self, q, interpolation)
   2450 
   2451         if is_scalar(q):
-> 2452             return self._get_cythonized_result(
   2453                 "group_quantile",
   2454                 aggregate=True,

.../python3.9/site-packages/pandas/core/groupby/groupby.py in _get_cythonized_result(self, how, cython_dtype, aggregate, numeric_only, needs_counts, needs_values, needs_2d, needs_nullable, min_count, needs_mask, needs_ngroups, result_is_index, pre_processing, post_processing, **kwargs)
   2899                         )
   2900                         continue
-> 2901                 vals = vals.astype(cython_dtype, copy=False)
   2902                 if needs_2d:
   2903                     vals = vals.reshape((-1, 1))

TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a number, not 'NAType'
```

</details>

What is odd is that the quantile function works fine with if we avoid using groupby:

```python
df["y"].quantile(0.5)
```

<details>

```text
0.2
```

</details>

#### Problem description

I would have expected that change from the default `float64` type to `pd.Float64Dtype` should produce the same results with the `NAN` values being treated in the same way.

review_comments: can you do a case with a listlike qs e.g. [0.5, 0.75]
Can you also check the case without the `["y"]`
any reason for "float" instead of np.float64?

actually I have picked this from the code around. Entire definition of `pre_processor` is like this.
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/a6943ae49f79452da6ca5f1c3e008ded4e0e2c85/pandas/core/groupby/groupby.py#L2435-L2459
OK.  not a big deal, can probably do a followup to change a bunch of non-explicit dtypes to np.float64
since we dont cast float32-> float64, I think we should cast Float32->float32 right?

actually I think we cast float32 to float64. When calling `_get_cythonized_result` we pass the below:
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/8814de9fbc7d53c6db201eab717fd3d6b607654b/pandas/core/groupby/groupby.py#L2474 
Below is the behaviour, I am getting on master.
```python

In [7]: df = pd.DataFrame({
   ...:     "x": [1, 1],
   ...:     "y": [0.2, np.nan]
   ...: }, dtype="float32")

In [8]: df.groupby("x")["y"].quantile(0.5)

x
```
